_about: The only differences between the TypeScript and Rust CLIs that are allowed (VE-3664). `accepted` documents the rules built into parity/lib.mjs, so the harness never reports them. `paths` lists JSON paths per command that may differ, and `rows` lists table/text rows (by regex on the row text), and `keyCasing` names command outputs whose nested keys print as the API sends them (snake_case) where the TS client camelCased them; the harness camelCases the Rust output for those and still requires every value to match. Each has a reason. Anything else is a defect. Goal (Yalcin, 2026-10-04): it works exactly like today's CLI, just faster.

accepted.reason: clap's standard help format replaces commander's (Yalcin, 2026-10-04). The harness still requires the same flags and subcommands.
Accepted by Yalcin, 2026-10-04. Tables are compared cell by cell.
clap convention, accepted by Yalcin, 2026-10-04. The harness never sends invalid arguments, so it doesn't exercise this.
It used to go to stdout and break `--json | jq` when an update was available. stderr is not compared.
Accepted by Yalcin, 2026-10-05 (VE-3727). Commander read --version anywhere as the global version flag, so the TS CLI printed its own version instead of installing <v>.
Accepted by Yalcin, 2026-10-05 (VE-3727). The TS CLI printed "Stopped watching." at once but kept running until the current poll interval ended.

accepted.what: OAuth `apps create` exits right after the callback
accepted.reason: Accepted by Yalcin, 2026-10-05 (VE-3727). The TS CLI kept polling the OAuth session after the browser callback had already settled the result.

accepted.what: A clean `Error:` line where the TS CLI crashed
accepted.reason: Accepted by Yalcin, 2026-10-05 (VE-3727). Where TS threw outside runAction (file reads, "Nothing to update", catalog role lookups) Node printed a stack trace or a TypeError; Rust prints `Error: <message>` and exits 1.

accepted.what: Error colour is decided from stderr
accepted.reason: Accepted by Yalcin, 2026-10-05 (VE-3727). The TS CLI coloured `Error:` when stdout was a terminal; Rust when stderr, the stream it writes to, is one.

accepted.what: No `- Fetching…` fallback line when stderr is redirected
accepted.reason: Accepted by Yalcin, 2026-10-05 (VE-3727). ora printed a static line when it could not animate; the Rust spinner stays silent. stderr is not compared.

accepted.what: `CI` and an unknown `TERM` don't turn colours off
accepted.reason: Accepted by Yalcin, 2026-10-05 (VE-3727). chalk's detection turned colours off for them; the Rust CLI colours whenever the stream is a terminal (NO_COLOR and FORCE_COLOR still apply).
Accepted by Yalcin, 2026-10-05 (VE-3727). indicatif draws it instead of ora, on stderr, which is not compared.

accepted.what: `--debug` request_failed shows the full error chain
accepted.reason: Deliberate since VE-3667; Accepted by Yalcin, 2026-10-05 (VE-3727). undici said only "fetch failed"; the chain names the cause (DNS, refused connection, TLS).

accepted.what: The update notice compares versions as semver
accepted.reason: Decided by Yalcin, 2026-10-05 (VE-3727). Only a strictly newer, non-pre-release version is announced, so an rc tester isn't told to "update" to the older stable release; the TS CLI announced any version that differed.

accepted.what: TLS uses the OS trust store; NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS is ignored
accepted.reason: ❓ Accepted by Yalcin, 2026-10-05 (VE-3727). rustls with the platform verifier (macOS keychain, the system CA store on Linux) replaces Node's bundled CA list; confirm with Yalcin.

accepted.what: Null or corrupt config values the TS CLI crashed on
accepted.reason: Accepted by Yalcin, 2026-10-05 (VE-3727). A null or wrongly typed value in config.json (for example "profiles": null) made the TS CLI throw; Rust treats it as unset.

paths.reason: The CLI binary check names the running executable, which is a different file for each CLI.
The PATH check names the running executable's directory.

rows.reason: These two checks name the running executable and its directory, which differ between the CLIs.

The Schedule row prints the integration's schedule object as the API sends it (snake_case keys, matching `--json`); the TS client camelCased it. ❓ Verbatim here is an assumption pending Yalcin. The values are still compared through the `integrations get --json` keyCasing rule.
